A.explanation: Point-by-point addition gives a deep trough on the left, a shallower trough in the middle and the tall positive peak on the right.

B.explanation: A flat line would need equal positive and negative displacement everywhere, but the tall positive peak has nothing to cancel it.

C.explanation: The left and middle sections cannot have the same depth because the left adds two negative displacements while the middle adds only one.

D.explanation: The left and middle sections cannot stay at the original shallow depth because the overlapping negative pulses reinforce to give a deeper resultant on the left.

hints: Notice the left-moving signal has one wide negative trough while the right-moving signal has a narrow negative trough followed by a tall positive peak.
Recall the principle of superposition: at each point the resultant displacement is the vector sum $x = x_1 + x_2$, keeping the sign of upward positive and downward negative.
Compare the three vertical sections when centred: left trough on trough, middle baseline on trough, and tall peak on baseline.
walkthrough: Identify the two shapes at the instant of complete overlap with centres together: the right-moving pulse contributes $-a$ then $0$ then $+b$, and the left-moving pulse contributes $-a$ over the first two sections and $0$ over the peak section.
State the rule: resultant displacement $x = x_1 + x_2$ at every point along the overlap, so negative plus negative gives a larger negative and positive plus zero stays positive.
Add section by section: left section $(-a)+(-a) = -2a$ is the deepest trough, middle section $(0)+(-a) = -a$ is a shallower trough, right section $(+b)+(0) = +b$ is the unchanged tall peak.
Check against the distractors: complete cancellation to zero is impossible, and equal-depth troughs ignore the double negative on the left.
This combined shape of deep left dip, half-depth middle step and tall right peak is option A.
